The cash flow tab reads it: insurance and card fees carry no sales tax, and wages, depreciation and interest carry none either.

c0330: The same calendar as the P&L and the scenarios

c0339: The P&L fixed costs without depreciation (which is not paid in cash) and WITH principal repaid (which is). This is the threshold that decides whether cash holds up

To turn a menu price into a price excl. sales tax, divide it by 1 + your sales tax rate (with an 8% rate, divide by 1.08); if an item is taxed at a different rate (alcohol to go, for instance), use that rate. The rate of each sales line is in the "Sales tax rate on the line (%)" column of the P&L, and from it come the receipts, the sales tax collected and the equivalent menu price incl. sales tax. With the default 0% recoverable input tax, the sales tax you pay on purchases and startup costs is treated as a cost; in the UK, enter 20% if you are VAT-registered.

c0442: Total startup costs (sum of the blocks)
c0547: The P&L tells you whether the business makes money; this tab tells you whether you have cash left to get to the end of the month. It is the first one a lender looks at.
c0562: Profile for your area: adjust it to your own slow and busy months (weather, tourism, events). It must add up to 100%
c0564: Rises in a straight line from the month-1 percentage to 100% over the number of months you set in Assumptions. With month 1 at 100%, the ramp disappears
c0566: Seasonality × ramp-up, normalized to 100%: the YEAR brings in what the P&L says, but split the way a business that has just opened would split it
c0569: The month's sales plus the sales tax collected, adjusted by the average collection days from the Assumptions tab
c0571: Purchases and variable costs (incl. sales tax)
c0573: The fixed costs that leave cash, each with its own tax rate: insurance carries none
c0575: Twelve monthly installments plus extra pay periods in the months you set in Assumptions (only if pay periods > 12). The total for the year is the same as the P&L's
c0579: Each sales line at ITS OWN rate, read from the sales tax column of the P&L (alcohol to go has its own rate cell in the Assumptions tab)
c0581: Each item at its own rate, read from the tax column of the P&L: insurance and card processing fees carry none
c0583: Sales tax paid on STARTUP COSTS enters here: it is offset against the tax collected in later quarters until used up. With 0% recoverable input tax (the US default) this line stays at zero
c0585: Sales tax collected minus recoverable input tax for the quarter, minus what was carried forward. If negative, nothing is paid: it is offset in the next quarter. With 0% recoverable input tax (the US default) it equals the sales tax collected in the quarter
c0587: Cash only leaves when the quarter's result is positive. Months without a settlement are left blank, not zero. The cell turns RED when the payment takes more cash than is left that month. The model settles quarterly (April, July, October, January): if your state requires monthly filing, expect smaller payments every month instead
c0591: If negative, raise working capital or the loan: you run out of cash
c0593: It answers the question that decides a bank deal: in which month the cash runs out
c0595: Free cash flow before debt, year 1
c0596: Net income plus depreciation (which is not paid) plus that year's interest: principal is not subtracted because this flow is BEFORE debt. The SAME basis as years 2 and 3, so the payback compares like with like
c0597: Free cash flow before debt, year 2
c0598: Net income plus depreciation (which is not paid) plus that year's interest: principal is not subtracted because this flow is BEFORE debt. Without a monthly table, it is an estimate
c0599: Free cash flow before debt, year 3
c0600: For reference: ACTUAL year-1 cash flow (monthly table, before debt)
c0601: The sum of the twelve monthly net cash flows above, adding back the interest and principal paid that year. It is NOT the one the payback uses: it includes sales tax not yet settled and supplier credit, two things that have to be paid back and that years 2 and 3 do not have
c0602: Investment to recover (net of recoverable input tax)
c0603: CAPEX plus working capital: the total cash needed MINUS the recoverable input tax on startup costs, which is not lost (it is recovered through the quarterly return, and this tab offsets it quarter by quarter; it is zero in the US default). Working capital is recovered when you close, but until then it is tied up
c0604: Measures how long the business takes to repay the investment with what it generates BEFORE paying the lender, on the SAME cash flow basis in all three years. Whether you can afford the loan payment is shown by the DSCR in the Financing tab
c0605: Payback on CAPEX, excluding working capital (years)
c0606: The same calculation on what you BUY (build-out, equipment, launch and formation costs), without working capital: that money is not spent, it is tied up and comes back when the business closes. For reference only: the payback that matters is the one above
c0607: Fourth-quarter sales tax is settled in January of the following year, so it does not appear in this table. The model pays year-1 income tax in July of year 2 (a simplification: estimated tax payments are usually quarterly). The loan payment is spread in twelve equal parts following the ANNUAL schedule in the Financing tab, and payroll in twelve monthly installments (plus extra pay periods in their month, only if pay periods > 12).
c0610: What you need, where it comes from and what it costs to repay. It is the sheet your lender asks for along with the P&L.
c0613: Loan requested — bank or SBA 7(a) (amortized below)
c0615: A source of funds only: NOT amortized, so it is not in the schedule, the P&L interest or the DSCR. Enter your bank or SBA 7(a) loan in row 7 ("Loan requested" in "0. Assumptions"); use this row only for a second loan
c0617: SBA Microloans go up to $50,000 through nonprofit intermediaries. Like row 8, a source of funds only: not in the schedule or the DSCR. If it is your only loan, enter it in row 7 instead
c0619: Equity: it dilutes your ownership and is not repaid
c0621: Usually paid AFTER you document the spending
c0624: Startup costs plus any recoverable tax you have to advance (zero by default in the US)
c0626: In red (negative), the plan is NOT funded. Far above zero is not free either: you pay interest on money you do not use
c0628: Amber above the margin you set: it is debt you pay for without needing it
c0630: A small cushion over the need is healthy; 20% extra is interest thrown away
c0631: Loan that would match sources to needs
c0632: Copy it into "Loan requested" in the "0. Assumptions" tab and the difference goes to zero. Rows 8-11 lower this figure, but only the row-7 loan is amortized and counted in the DSCR
c0637: An interest-only period equal to or longer than the term does not exist: the sheet cancels it at the source
c0639: Standard amortizing loan with a level annual payment. At a 0% rate it is the principal divided by the repayment years: without that branch the schedule would shut down entirely
c0647: Cash flow available for debt service (after tax; from year 4 on, year 3 held flat)
c0650: Rounding margin. Above it, the schedule does not close and there is principal left unpaid
c0652: Must be zero: the principal repaid in the schedule has to equal the amount borrowed. If it is positive, the term falls short
c0661: An INTEREST-ONLY year, if there is one: with only interest in the denominator the ratio shoots up and does not measure the business
c0664: Minimum DSCR across the whole schedule
c0665: The worst year of the life of the loan, not the best of the three the P&L projects. It is the number that decides a loan. Mind the scope: years 1 to 3 come from the P&L, and from year 4 on the schedule HOLDS year 3's cash flow, so the minimum over those years is a sustained projection, not a calculated year. The cash flow is after tax
c0666: DSCR is calculated BEFORE debt and AFTER tax: income tax is subtracted from pre-tax income, depreciation and interest are added back, and the result is divided by what has to be paid that year. Below the minimum in the "0. Assumptions" tab, the business does not generate enough to repay the loan. In the schedule, the available cash flow from year 4 on is held at year 3's: the P&L projects only three years, and no growth is invented here that has not been calculated.
